item.title: Human Rights Watch: AI Strategy and Solutions Lead (one-year fixed term)
item.description:
Organisation: Human Rights Watch (HRW), Operations Department

Location: Must be within commuting distance of an HRW office: Amsterdam, Amman, Berlin, Brussels, London, Stockholm, New York, Washington DC, Miami, Sao Paulo, Toronto or Chicago. Reports to the Chief Information Officer in Berlin. No relocation support and no work-authorisation sponsorship.

Award: USD 102,000 to 112,000 plus employer-paid benefits if based in the US; ranges outside the US are set by local market conditions. No application fee.

Duration: One year fixed-term, full time. Application deadline 30 August 2026.

Deadline: 30 Aug 2026

Human Rights Watch is hiring an AI Strategy and Solutions Lead into its Operations Department to build the foundation for responsible AI adoption across the organisation. The role deliberately sits between strategy and execution: assessing organisational readiness, mapping partnerships and governance, and also prototyping and shipping working systems. THE WORK, in four strands. (1) STRATEGY AND READINESS: with the CIO and the Information Security and Technology (IST) leadership team, build an AI strategy covering data foundation requirements, infrastructure gaps and organisational readiness; assess current state and shape a roadmap balancing quick wins against long-term capacity; research what peer nonprofit, humanitarian and human rights organisations are doing and find collaboration openings. (2) FLAGSHIP SOLUTIONS: work with departments to find high-impact use cases, translate business needs into technical approaches, build and deploy AI/ML solutions with measurable value (time saved, efficiency, better outcomes), using the Microsoft AI ecosystem (Copilot Studio, Azure AI, Power Platform) among other tools, and oversee consultants and vendors to extend delivery capacity. (3) ADOPTION AND CAPACITY: balance onboarding staff onto AI tools against building custom solutions where they amplify the organisation's strengths; write training material pitched at different work areas and skill levels covering prompting and responsible use; support working groups and communities of practice; produce playbooks and guides for non-technical staff. (4) GOVERNANCE: partner with IST leadership on risk assessment frameworks, align solutions with security, infrastructure and architecture requirements, contribute to AI policy development and its operationalisation, set standards for evaluating proofs of concept and MVPs, and engage business units so outcomes are co-owned; all of it balanced against data quality, security and resource constraints and HRW's mission as a human rights organisation. WHO THEY WANT: a bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience in computer science, data science, information systems, mathematics, AI/ML implementation or a related technical field; a minimum of seven years' relevant experience including two to three years on AI and two to three years implementing AI/ML in production; experience contributing to technology strategy and assessing organisational readiness for new technology; strong Python and ML library/framework skills; hands-on predictive modelling, data science and statistical analysis; experience with low-code/no-code AI platforms such as Copilot Studio or Power Platform; a track record of scoping and delivering under resource constraints; a grasp of both generative AI and traditional ML; and the ability to explain technical concepts plainly to mixed audiences, engage stakeholders and lead technology adoption as an internal partner to business teams. PREFERRED: nonprofit, humanitarian or human rights experience; data privacy, security and ethical AI knowledge; familiarity with responsible AI frameworks and governance models; vendor and consultant management; and a background in politically sensitive or high-risk environments. APPLY: through the HRW job portal with a cover letter and CV, preferably as PDFs, by 30 August 2026. Only complete applications are reviewed and only shortlisted candidates are contacted; no calls or email enquiries. HRW states that it does not discriminate on the basis of disability, age, gender identity and expression, national origin, race and ethnicity, religious beliefs, sexual orientation or criminal record.

item.title: Fonds BJP: Dossiersubsidie for Freelance Regional and Local Journalists (autumn 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Fonds Bijzondere Journalistieke Projecten (Fonds BJP)

Location: Netherlands; for freelance journalists working on Dutch regional and local reporting

Award: Up to EUR 19,200 for six months of work on a single reporting dossier. No application fee.

Duration: Six months of dedicated reporting on one subject area

Deadline: 14 Sep 2026

The Dossiersubsidie is the Fonds BJP scheme for freelance regional and local journalists in the Netherlands who want to follow one subject properly rather than chase daily news, funding up to EUR 19,200 for six months of sustained reporting on a single dossier. It is aimed at the gap left by shrinking regional newsrooms, where structural coverage of local government, housing, care or industry rarely gets paid time. ELIGIBILITY: freelance journalists working in Dutch regional and local media only (staff journalists and national-only reporters are directed to the fund's other schemes). The fund also runs a year-round Vooronderzoekssubsidie of up to EUR 8,800 for preliminary research and a year-round Uitvoeringssubsidie of up to EUR 38,600 for carrying out projects, both open to all journalists. APPLICATION WINDOW: 17 August to 14 September 2026, via the Fonds BJP subsidy portal. Online office hours on 8 September 2026; questions on 020 63 86 295.

item.title: University of Twente: Postdoc, Ethics and Epistemology of LLMs4EU (17 months)
item.description:
Organisation: University of Twente, Philosophy section / 4TU.Center for Ethics and Technology

Location: Enschede, Netherlands

Award: EUR 4,241 to 5,538 gross per month (scale 10, steps 4 to 12) at 1.0 FTE, plus 8 percent holiday allowance and an 8.3 percent year-end bonus.

Duration: 17 months, full-time (38 to 40 hours per week), with possible extension

Deadline: Closed 25 Aug 2026

A postdoctoral position in the Philosophy section at the University of Twente, part of the 4TU.Center for Ethics and Technology, working on the ethics and epistemology strand (Work Package 6) of LLMs4EU. LLMs4EU is a European Commission funded initiative led by the Alliance for Language Technologies, spanning more than 20 countries, to build large language models across all EU languages and preserve European linguistic and cultural diversity in the digital age while keeping the resulting tools compliant with European values and legislation including the AI Act and the GDPR. TASKS: establish benchmarking frameworks that address legal and ethical concerns; develop guidelines for fine-tuning processes with an emphasis on preserving cultural heritage; oversee ethics compliance and advise the project ethics board; and build frameworks that integrate ethical considerations into LLM design. This is the tech-communication and language-politics end of AI research rather than a modelling job: the questions are whose language, whose culture and whose norms get encoded when a continent builds its own models. REQUIREMENTS: a doctorate in ethics, philosophy, science and technology studies, AI ethics, computer science with an ethics focus, or a related field; demonstrated expertise in AI ethics and ethics compliance; understanding of AI tool design and LLM development; appreciation for cultural diversity; strong communication and organisational skills; and professional English. Apply through the AcademicTransfer posting. Closes 25 August 2026.

item.title: Utrecht University: PhD, Media and Democracy in the 1970s (NWO Vidi project)
item.description:
Organisation: Utrecht University, Faculty of Humanities, Department of History and Art History

Location: Utrecht, Netherlands (Drift 6)

Award: EUR 3,059 to 3,881 gross per month at 36 to 40 hours per week, on the Dutch university PhD scale, plus 8 percent holiday allowance and 8.3 percent year-end bonus. No application fee.

Duration: 18-month initial contract, extended to four years after a positive first-year assessment

Deadline: 06 Sep 2026

Fully funded PhD position in the NWO-funded Vidi project 'Democracy and the (de-)regulation of the media in Europe since the 1970s', which reads the contestation and transformation of democracy in the last quarter of the twentieth century through media governance. This sub-project examines how social movements, pirate broadcasters and alternative media initiatives challenged the public broadcasting monopoly across Western Europe during the long 1970s, drawing on archival research. REQUIREMENTS: a master's degree in history or a related field, a demonstrated interest in the history of democracy and media governance, professional English plus at least one other European language, archival research experience and a collaborative approach. Apply through the AcademicTransfer posting (vacancy number 5535). Project leader Dr Pepijn Corduwener (p.corduwener@uu.nl). Deadline 6 September 2026.

item.title: Cultuurloket DigitALL: Pilot Contribution (Pilotbijdrage, 2026-2027, rolling)
item.description:
Organisation: Cultuurloket DigitALL (successor to Kickstart Cultuurfonds)

Location: Netherlands and the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom. No city or region restriction.

Award: Up to EUR 75,000. Covers pilot development, audience testing, and knowledge development or training via partner organisations if budgeted. Hardware-only purchases are not eligible. No stated co-financing percentage. No application fee. Annual donation budget of EUR 1.9 million in 2026 and 2027.

Duration: Not fixed; scoped to pilot, prototype or first live version development. Scheme runs through the end of 2027.

Deadline: Rolling / undated

Cultuurloket DigitALL funds the digital innovation of the Dutch cultural sector and is the strongest dedicated digital-culture route currently open to Dutch cultural organisations. It is the successor to the discontinued Kickstart Cultuurfonds, backed by the VandenEnde Foundation, VSBfonds, Ammodo, Het Cultuurfonds and others. The pilot contribution of up to EUR 75,000 supports developing and running a first pilot, prototype or live version of a digital tool, which covers a wide range of creative-technology work embedded in festivals, exhibitions and public programmes. Eligible applicants are theatres, music venues, film theatres, museums, festivals and professional performing arts producers, with collaborations between institutions given priority. The pilot must be tested with the intended public audience, not only with experts, and funding cannot be used exclusively for hardware acquisition. Applications go through an online portal with no deadline and are handled in order of receipt. TIMING: a decision follows within ten weeks of submission, so plan roughly three months of lead time between applying and project start. Training and knowledge development through partner organisations is only covered when included in the submitted budget, so build it in from the outset.

item.title: Cultuurloket DigitALL: Implementation Contribution (Implementatiebijdrage, 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Cultuurloket DigitALL

Location: Netherlands and the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom. No city or region restriction.

Award: Up to EUR 30,000. Covers technical modification, system integration, production and deployment costs. Hardware purchase alone is ineligible unless clearly essential to the public experience. No stated co-financing percentage. No application fee.

Duration: Not specified; scoped to a single implementation.

Deadline: 01 Nov 2026

A one-off 2026 call letting Dutch cultural institutions reuse and adapt digital technology that other institutions have already built and published in the open DigitALL Toolkit, for example translation software shared between theatres or a streaming platform adapted for a new venue. Grants run up to EUR 30,000 and cover technical modification, integration, production and deployment costs. Eligible applicants are museums, theatres, music venues, festivals, film theatres and professional performing arts producers. Applications are submitted online and assessed in order of receipt rather than comparatively, with a decision within ten weeks. The deadline was extended from 31 May 2026 to 1 November 2026 after high demand. IMPORTANT RESTRICTION: this route cannot be used to further develop your own pilot internally; it exists specifically to spread another institution's working technology across the sector. For developing something new, use the DigitALL pilot contribution instead.

item.title: University of Amsterdam: PhD, Protest and Political Speech in the Nordics 1930-1970 (Sound of Disagreement)
item.description:
Organisation: University of Amsterdam (UvA), Faculty of Humanities, Department of European Studies

Location: Amsterdam, Netherlands (Kloveniersburgwal 48)

Award: EUR 3,059 to 3,881 gross per month at 38 hours per week, on the Dutch university PhD scale, plus 8 percent holiday allowance and 8.3 percent year-end bonus. No application fee.

Duration: 48 months full-time (16-month initial contract, extended by 32 months after a positive evaluation); preferred start 1 January 2027

Deadline: Closed 20 Aug 2026

Fully funded four-year PhD position within 'The Sound of Disagreement: Embodied Histories of Political Speech 1800-present', an interdisciplinary project on how political groups have argued in public and how disagreement sounds. This sub-project covers Nordic labour movements and the articulation of protest from roughly 1930 to 1970, explicitly working on the sonic practices of political debate and the mediatization of protest, so it suits researchers with a sound studies, media studies or oral history angle as much as historians. REQUIREMENTS: a master's degree in History, European Studies, Media Studies, Nordic Studies or a related discipline; fluency in Danish, Finnish, Norwegian or Swedish depending on the chosen case study; professional English; archival research skills; and a collaborative disposition. Apply via the AcademicTransfer posting (vacancy number 15290) with a motivation letter, CV and research statement. Deadline 20 August 2026.

item.title: University of Twente: Postdoc, Multimodal Conversational AI for Cultural Heritage
item.description:
Organisation: University of Twente, Human Media Interaction group

Location: Enschede, Netherlands

Award: EUR 3,546 to 5,538 gross per month for 40 hours per week (8 salary steps, depending on experience), plus standard Dutch university holiday and year-end allowances.

Duration: One year, renewable for a further two years subject to positive evaluation; 40 hours per week

Deadline: Closed 16 Aug 2026

A postdoctoral position in the Human Media Interaction group at the University of Twente on the project 'Balancing Personalisation and Polyvocality: Dialogic Interaction for Open-mindedness and Empathy in Conversational AI'. The work develops and evaluates multimodal conversational agents for museum settings that hold personalisation in tension with exposure to plural perspectives, rather than optimising for engagement alone. Tasks include building models that use gaze, speech and dialogue data to infer visitor engagement and openness, designing adaptive dialogue strategies, running VR-based user studies, and publishing in strong venues. Of the current Dutch academic postings this is the closest thing to a funded creative-technologist brief: museum interpretation, multimodal sensing and dialogue design in one role. REQUIREMENTS: a PhD in computer science, AI, HCI or a related field; experience with conversational AI, dialogue systems or adaptive systems; experience running empirical research, preferably user studies; strong analytical and academic writing skills; and excellent English. Apply with a CV including publications, a motivation letter and two academic references. Contact: Shenghui Wang (shenghui.wang@utwente.nl). NOTE: the AcademicTransfer listing page shows a 16 August 2026 deadline while the detail page states 17 August 2026, so treat 16 August as the effective cut-off.

item.title: GLINA3: Open Call for a Collaborator Working with Type, Language and Visual Systems
item.description:
Organisation: GLINA3

Location: Amsterdam, Netherlands (studio is Amsterdam-based; collaboration terms not specified)

Award: Paid collaboration. The studio states the fee will be confirmed upon successful funding, so the amount is contingent and not published up front. No application fee.

Duration: New collaborative research project, length not specified

Deadline: Closed 12 Aug 2026

GLINA3 is an Amsterdam clay 3D printing and digital design studio, and it is looking for one collaborator to join a new research project at the intersection of typography, language, technology and material culture. They want an artist, writer, poet, anthropologist or artistic researcher whose existing practice already engages with type design, typography, writing systems, visual language, fonts and letterforms, language technologies, or the tools that shape how language is produced, read or translated. This is an unusually good fit for anyone working on the machine-readable side of language: the brief explicitly names language technologies and translation tooling alongside classical type design. ELIGIBILITY: individual practitioners with demonstrable work in one or more of the listed areas. HOW TO APPLY: the studio asks for relevant work, research, publications or projects connected to type, fonts, writing systems, visual language or the tools that shape them, and nothing else. Because the deadline is tight they say Instagram DM is the fastest route; you can also email a short introduction and one relevant project to office@glina3.nl. NOTE: the fee is confirmed only if the project's own funding comes through, so clarify terms before committing time.

item.title: Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences: Digital Life Researcher (Embodied AI Rehabilitation Agents)
item.description:
Organisation: Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences (Hogeschool van Amsterdam)

Location: Amsterdam, Netherlands (Weesperzijde campus), on site

Duration: Full-time, 40 hours per week

Deadline: Closed 30 Jul 2026

A junior researcher post in the Digital Life research group at the Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences, working on embodied AI rehabilitation agents that support patients during rehabilitation and recovery in everyday life. The programme sits at the intersection of human-centred AI, digital health and rehabilitation technology, and the role is unusually hands-on for a research job: co-designing rehabilitation technologies with patients and healthcare professionals, building interactive prototypes with sensing technologies and embodied interaction, running user-centred evaluations in real-world living lab settings, and contributing to scientific reports and presentations. REQUIREMENTS: a master's degree in human-computer interaction, industrial design, computer science, software engineering, AI or a related field; demonstrated research experience including co-design and evaluation with diverse stakeholders; experience designing interactive prototypes with sensing or embodied systems; sensor data collection, processing and analysis skills; and programming in Python, JavaScript or comparable languages. Excellent written and spoken English is required and Dutch proficiency is preferred. Apply with a CV and motivation letter through the application portal. item.title: AIxDESIGN x KB: Open Call for Sessions, (Art)works and Performances
item.description:
Organisation: AIxDESIGN, co-presented with the Koninklijke Bibliotheek (KB), National Library of the Netherlands

Location: KB, The Hague, Netherlands (in-person exhibition and programme); pitches welcome from people based anywhere

Award: Fees by track: opening-night experience EUR 1,500 to 2,000; a session in the events programme EUR 2,000 to 2,500; an existing (art)work for the exhibition EUR 200 to 400 honorarium (including licensing and production). The fee stays the same wherever you are based.

Duration: Exhibition runs November 2026 to February 2027; opening event November 2026

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

AIxDESIGN and the KB (Koninklijke Bibliotheek, the National Library of the Netherlands) are building an exhibition and public programme about AI, made from the national collection, at the KB in The Hague. Nadia Piet is Creative Lead with the AIxDESIGN community, co-presented with the KB. The premise: long before neural nets, libraries were the machines we built to organise human knowledge, and the show uses the KB's collection to look at what AI is, where it comes from, and how it connects to the older story of how we store, sort, and search what we know. Part of the show lives in the KB Atelier, with talks, workshops, and screenings alongside, intended as AI literacy you can wander into. WHAT THEY WANT: work that engages AI in some way (critical, creative, hands-on, or playful); bonus if it also speaks to archives, libraries, or how we store and sort knowledge, though you do not need to touch the KB's collection to take part. You may pitch to more than one track: (A) SOMETHING FOR THE OPENING NIGHT, a performance, talk, screening, tour, ritual, booth, game, or other experience for the November 2026 opening, fee EUR 1,500 to 2,000; (B) A SESSION IN THE EVENTS PROGRAMME, a workshop or other session once during the three-month run, around 2.5 to 4 hours, fee EUR 2,000 to 2,500; (C) AN (ART)WORK FOR THE EXHIBITION, existing work in any format (installation, sculpture, zine stand, a corner of your own) sturdy enough for a public area with daily traffic, honorarium EUR 200 to 400 including licensing and production; (D) SOMETHING ELSE ENTIRELY, pitch it anyway. WHO: artists, designers, researchers, technologists, performers, musicians, archivists, or educators working around AI, data, libraries, or cultural heritage; no finished idea or polished CV needed, just a clear, specific pitch. You can be based anywhere and they especially welcome people outside the Netherlands; the show is in-person in The Hague and the fee stays the same wherever you are coming from. HOW TO APPLY: send a short pitch through the form (which track, your idea in a paragraph or two, roughly what it would need, and a link to your work); takes about five minutes, no full application required. Deadline: end of August 2026. Questions to hello@aixdesign.co.

Open call details

item.title: KB Researcher-in-Residence (RiR) 2027
item.description:
Organisation: KB, National Library of the Netherlands

Location: The Hague, Netherlands (two days per week on-site at the KB premises)

Award: Secondment at 0.5 FTE for 6 months based on your current salary, up to EUR 5,590 gross per month for a full-time-equivalent position, plus travel expenses, office facilities, and support from a research software engineer, research advisor, and collection and data specialists. No application fee.

Duration: 6 months at 0.5 FTE (two days per week on-site); two positions in 2027, starting Q1 and Q3

Deadline: 27 Sep 2026

ELIGIBILITY: two Researcher-in-Residence positions in 2027. Open to early-career researchers of any discipline (data science, social science, computer science, humanities) who are currently working on a PhD or within 5 years of their PhD end date. You must have, or be able to secure, an affiliation with a Dutch university or research institute willing to second you; external PhD students may use the funding to obtain such a contract. Your project must make use of one or more of the KB digital collections and you must be able to work with primarily Dutch data. You must be available at 0.5 FTE over 6 months and able to spend two days a week on-site at the KB in The Hague. COLLECTIONS: over 130 million digitized pages of newspapers, magazines, radio bulletins and books from 1470 onward (via Delpher and DBNL), a born-digital web collection of more than 23,000 websites, ground-truth and derived datasets on the KB Lab, and metadata including Linked Data. APPLY: use the official proposal template and submit a single PDF by 27 September 2026 to dh@kb.nl, after reading the call's terms and conditions; questions to dh@kb.nl. TIMELINE: deadline 27 September 2026; internal eligibility review followed by an external committee review; outcome notified November 2026; residencies start Q1 and Q3 2027. DISCIPLINES: digital humanities / data science / computational research with cultural-heritage collections. NOTE: the output is usually a dataset or tool prototype hosted on the KB Lab; you agree to share results via blog posts on the KB Lab and to publish resulting tools or data under an open license within 6 months of the residency. Proposals should align with the KB Research Agenda or the Cultural AI Lab.

item.title: WBSO: R&D Tax Credit (rolling, Netherlands)
item.description:
Organisation: Rijksdienst voor Ondernemend Nederland (RVO)

Location: Netherlands. Dutch companies and self-employed paying payroll or income tax that conduct qualifying R&D.

Award: Payroll/income tax reduction for R&D, not a cash grant. 2026: 36 percent of the first EUR 380,000 of R&D wage costs (50 percent for startups), 16 percent above; fixed deduction for self-employed. National budget EUR 1.817 billion for 2026. No application fee.

Duration: Applied for in advance per period; cannot start before approval.

Deadline: Rolling / undated

The WBSO (Wet Bevordering Speur- en Ontwikkelingswerk) is the Dutch R&D tax credit administered by RVO. It reduces payroll/wage tax for companies with R&D staff and provides an income-tax deduction for self-employed people doing R&D; it is a tax credit, not a cash grant. For 2026 the benefit is 36 percent of the first EUR 380,000 of R&D wage and other costs (50 percent for qualifying startups) and 16 percent above that; self-employed receive a fixed deduction (and need at least 500 R&D hours per year). Eligible applicants are Dutch companies and self-employed people paying payroll or income tax who carry out qualifying R&D in the EU. Applications are made in advance via Mijn RVO and cannot be retroactive; for coverage of the final three months of a year the deadline is 30 September. Time-keeping and project administration are required. No application fee.

item.title: Jan van Eyck Food Lab Fellowship 2027
item.description:
Organisation: Jan van Eyck Academie (with Maastricht University and Creative Europe Institution(ing)s project)

Location: Maastricht, Netherlands (Fellow must reside within 10 km of Maastricht; fieldwork in Venlo with travel covered up to EUR 750)

Award: Monthly stipend of EUR 1,750 (80 percent income-tax exempt), annual working budget of EUR 2,250, plus local transport costs to and from Venlo up to EUR 750 covered by Maastricht University. EUR 50 + VAT application fee (waived for applicants from DAC list Least Developed / Low-Income / Lower-Middle-Income Countries and for Palestinian artists).

Duration: 11 months, 15 January 2027 to 15 December 2027

Deadline: Closed 04 Jun 2026

ELIGIBILITY: one Fellow selected. Open to artists, designers, researchers, and interdisciplinary practitioners working in food, ecology, agriculture, and adjacent fields. The Fellow must reside in Maastricht or within a 10 km radius during the fellowship. APPLY: submit a single PDF (max 10 MB) via the online registration form containing a motivational letter and project proposal (max 500 words each), portfolio documentation (max 15 pages, 1-2 images per page, work from the past 5 years), and a CV (max 2 pages). All materials in English. Application fee EUR 50 + VAT paid via PayPal at submission; waived for DAC-list and Palestinian applicants. TIMELINE: deadline 4 June 2026; fellowship runs 15 January to 15 December 2027; results showcased at Jan van Eyck Open Studios in October 2027 and documented for the Institution(ing)s project. DISCIPLINES: food / ecology / interdisciplinary research-based practice. NOTE: the Fellow gets a private studio and access to the Academie's Labs, in-house experts, and guest advisers, and participates in the Institution(ing)s project alongside SES researchers and students at Maastricht University. Co-funded by Maastricht University and Creative Europe.

item.title: NWO: SSH Open Competition XS 2026 - Round 3
item.description:
Organisation: Dutch Research Council (NWO)

Location: Netherlands (applicants must be academic researchers affiliated to a Dutch knowledge institution)

Award: Up to EUR 50,000 per project

Duration: Project-based, typically 12-24 months

Deadline: 15 Sep 2026

Small curiosity-driven research grants in the social sciences and humanities, awarded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO). Round 3 of the 2026 SSH Open Competition XS closes 15 September 2026, 14:00 CEST. Up to EUR 50,000 per project to enable researchers to pursue novel, exploratory and high-risk ideas without the constraints of larger themed calls. ELIGIBILITY: academic researchers with an institutional affiliation at a Dutch university or recognised Dutch knowledge institute. Proposals are assessed on scientific quality and the potential for renewal of social-sciences and humanities research. Round 3 details and the dedicated application page will be published by NWO closer to the deadline; the linked page is the most recent SSH XS round, which is the same scheme.
